questions.question: What is the smallest three-digit number which, when divided by 8 or 6, leaves a remainder of 1 in each case?
questions.solution:
Given:

Smallest 3 - digit number leaves 1 remainder when divided by 8 or 6. 

Concept Used;

Lowest Common Multiple (L.C.M) 

The smallest three digit number is 100

Calculation:

L.C.M of 8 and 6 

⇒ Prime factorization

8 = 2 × 2 × 2

6 = 3 × 2

⇒ L.C.M = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24

When we divide 100 by 24 , we get 4 as the remainder 

The smallest three-digit number which is divisible by 8 or 6 = 100 - 4 + 24 = 120

The smallest three-digit number which when divided by 8 or 6 leaves remainder 1 in each case = (120 + 1) = 121.

Hence, the smallest three- digit number is 121.

questions.question: A 30-litre mixture of milk and water contains 15% water. How much water must be added to it to increase the percentage of water in the solution to 37.5%?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using **Alligation Method** by focusing on water percentage:

Water in **initial mixture** = 15% | Water added (pure) = 100% | **Target water** = 37.5%

Ratio of (Initial Mixture : Added Water) = (100 − 37.5) : (37.5 − 15) = 62.5 : 22.5 = **25 : 9**

Given, 25 units = **30 liters** ⇒ 1 unit = 1.2 liters

Added water = 9 units = 9 × 1.2 = **10.8 liters**

**∴ The correct answer is 10.8 liters.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial volume = **30 liters**, Initial Water = **15%**, Target Water = **37.5%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a63c313e6693be2a97847d0565bc6e2c1cd383da678853b3dcb46492ade707b2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the amount of **water to be added** be x liters.

⇒ In the mixture, **Milk** remains constant.

⇒ Initial **Milk percentage** = 100% − 15% = 85%.

⇒ Initial **quantity of Milk** = 85% of 30 = (85 ÷ 100) × 30 = 25.5 liters.

⇒ Final **Milk percentage** required = 100% − 37.5% = 62.5%.

⇒ Total **new volume** = (30 + x) liters.

⇒ 62.5% of (30 + x) = 25.5

⇒ 0.625 × (30 + x) = 25.5

⇒ 30 + x = 25.5 ÷ 0.625

⇒ 30 + x = 40.8

⇒ x = 40.8 − 30 = 10.8 liters.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.8 liters.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Quantity Concept

When only one component of a mixture is added or removed, the quantity of the other component remains unchanged. Use the formula: Initial Total × Initial % = Final Total × Final % for the constant part.

Rule of Alligation

It is a rule to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at their respective prices/concentrations must be mixed to produce a mixture at a given mean price/concentration.

Standard percentages like 37.5% can be written as 3/8, and 12.5% as 1/8 to speed up manual calculations during exams.</p

questions.question: What is the average of 12.5, 18.4, 15.5, 16.6, and 20.4?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **Assumed Mean** of 16.

Calculate **deviations** from 16: −3.5, +2.4, −0.5, +0.6, and +4.4.

Net deviation = (−3.5 − 0.5) + (2.4 + 0.6 + 4.4) = −4.0 + 7.4 = +3.4.

Average correction = Net deviation ÷ Total terms = 3.4 ÷ 5 = 0.68.

Actual Average = Assumed Mean + Correction = 16 + 0.68 = 16.68.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.68.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 12.5, 18.4, 15.5, 16.6, and 20.4.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb099920044e9d60cae89c86981fd15b63071bdfee0786b20ed7b2dcbae92785.png] 

⇒ Sum = 12.5 + 18.4 + 15.5 + 16.6 + 20.4

⇒ Sum = 83.4

⇒ Number of terms = 5

⇒ Average = 83.4 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 16.68

**∴ The correct answer is 16.68.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The **mean** (average) is the central value of a set of numbers, calculated as Sum ÷ Count.

Properties of Average

If each observation is increased or decreased by a **constant k**, the new average also increases or decreases by **k**.

Weighted Average

When sets have different sizes n₁ and n₂ with averages x₁ and x₂, the **combined average** is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

__
 
• **Seasonal une****mployment **occurs when people are unemployed at particular times of the year when demand for labour is lower than usual.
 
• **Seasonal unemployment refers to a temporary window of time **where the number of available employment opportunities decreases.
 
• **The cause of seasonal unemployment are Lack of multiple cropping, Lack of small-scale and cottage industries in rural areas, Lack of commercialisation of agriculture.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Types of Unemployment in India:

 
 
• Disguised Unemployment: 

 
 
• It is a phenomenon wherein more people are employed than actually needed.
 
• It is primarily traced in the agricultural and unorganised sectors of India.
 
 
 
• Seasonal Unemployment:
 
 
• It is unemployment that occurs during certain seasons of the year.
 
• Agricultural labourers in India rarely worked throughout the year.
 
 
 
• Cyclical Unemployment:
 
 
• It is the result of the business cycle, where unemployment rises during recessions and declines with economic growth.
 
• Cyclical unemployment figures in India are negligible.
 
• It is a phenomenon that is mostly found in capitalist economies.
 
 
 
• Technological Unemployment:
 
 
• It is the loss of jobs due to changes in technology.
 
• In 2016, World Bank data predicted that the proportion of jobs threatened by automation in India is 69% year-on-year.
 
 
 
• Frictional Unemployment:
 
 
• Frictional Unemployment also called Search Unemployment, refers to the time lag between the jobs when an individual is searching for a new job or is switching between the jobs.
 
• In other words, an employee requires time for searching for a new job or shifting from the existing to a new job, this inevitable time delay causes frictional unemployment.
 
• It is often considered voluntary unemployment because it is not caused due to the shortage of jobs, but in fact, the workers themselves quit their jobs in search of better opportunities.
 
 
 
• Vulnerable Employment:
 
 
• This means, people, working informally, without proper job contracts and thus sans any legal protection.
 
• These persons are deemed ‘unemployed’ since records of their work are never maintained.
 
• It is one of the main types of unemployment in India.
